public_rationale: METR's April 2025 evaluation places a pre-release o3 checkpoint at 50% predicted success on HCAST tasks taking humans about 1.5 hours [e1]. Its March 2025 study reports Claude 3.7 Sonnet's 50% success horizon at about 59 minutes and its 80% horizon at about 15 minutes of human task time [e2]. These results support the warning against expecting dependable complex-task completion in the evaluated deployment settings [e1, e2].
limitations: The evaluations use agent interfaces and do not directly test exclusively unassisted chat.
The o3 result concerns a pre-release checkpoint; the Claude result concerns 3.7 Sonnet.
The task suites differ, so the reported horizons are not directly comparable [e1].
The evidence does not cover every business problem or establish a capability ceiling.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: o3 or Claude cannot simply be dropped into complex problems and expected to work reliably.

statement.excerpt: What this means for business and society is that you can’t simply drop o3 or Claude into some complex problem and expect it to work reliably.

from_speaker: can’t simply drop o3 or Claude into some complex problem
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading warns against expecting dependable completion of arbitrary complex problems without task-specific engineering or oversight. It does not say every complex problem fails.
Basic interfaces that let a model act in an environment are relevant to simple deployment, but their results are not identical to unassisted chat.
Assess o3 and contemporaneous Claude versions separately; o3-mini is not a substitute for evidence about o3.
Use calendar 2025 through June 7 for contemporary capability reports because no period or regular reporting interval is specified.
Dropped into complex problems describes the deployment setting, not an antecedent for a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations of o3 and contemporaneous Claude versions show substantial failure rates on verifiable complex tasks without bespoke task solutions or continuing human correction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad evaluations demonstrate dependable completion of representative complex tasks by both named model families under simple deployment conditions.
